title: KV miniaturized quant + adaptive fallback probe
creator: Miguel Santos
description: Goal: evaluate aggressive KV cache size reductions by applying three compression modes (FP8, INT8, INT4) and a lightweight compaction layer, then quantify generation quality and tail-latency impacts. We need a pragmatic fallback policy so we can opportunistically shrink GPU KV footprint on tight memory hosts without exposing customer-visible regressions. This ticket runs end-to-end experiments, instruments metrics, and produces a recommended rollout plan (per-model, per-layer heuristics + runtime fallback).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Benchmarks for FP8/INT8/INT4 showing memory reduction and throughput gains on representative production profiles. 2) Quantified quality regressions (automatic metrics + small human eval) with thresholds and recommended per-model target. 3) Implementation of adaptive fallback prototype (quant-failure -> INT8 -> FP16 hotpath) with canary config. 4) Draft runtime config and rollout doc for runtime-1.18.
experiment_plan: Select three representative model families used in production (open-llama-13B, redwood-v1-7B-compat, and a 70B reference) and three workload profiles (short chat, long-context summarization, embedding+rerank).

Create deterministic prompt sets: 3k prompts for automated metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/KL/token-levenshtein), 200 prompts for targeted math/structured-output regression probes, and 150 sample pairs for blind human preference tests.
Implement conversion pipelines for FP8 (E4M3-like), symmetric INT8, and grouped INT4 packing in the KV cache serialization layer. Add optional per-layer scaling metadata.
Run closed-loop A/B baseline comparisons on 8xA100 and 4xH100 nodes to measure memory footprint, peak GPU memory during decode, sustained QPS at target latency SLOs, and token/sec improvements.
Collect quality signals: token-level cross-entropy delta, top-k KL divergence, answer exact-match on synthetic QA, and small human preference evaluation for >10% regression cases.
Instrument runtime fallback: live quant-check on KV materialization, automatic re-materialize to higher precision if decode loss exceeds threshold or if numeric instability observed.
Surface results in a cost/latency/quality trade-off dashboard and propose default conservative profiles for hosted vs dedicated customers.
updates: 2025-11-05: Prototype FP8 encoder implemented in serving runtime; initial unit tests pass for round-trip encoding/decoding with synthetic tensors.

2025-11-07: First memory sweep on llama-13B: FP8 reduces KV store by ~60% vs FP16, INT8 ~55%, int4 packed ~72% (excluding alignment overhead). Measured peak decode memory down ~35% on batched short-chat workloads.
2025-11-10: Quality smoke tests: automated cross-entropy delta shows median changes: FP8 +0.02 nats/token, INT8 +0.06 nats/token, INT4 +0.25 nats/token on conversational dataset (lower is better).

2025-11-12: Discovered instability on arithmetic/math prompts when using INT4 on higher layers; rare hallucination increase observed in 8/200 test prompts. Scoped to a subset of attention heads in layer 28-32 for the 70B reference.

2025-11-14: Built adaptive per-layer bitmask where bottom N layers use INT4, middle layers INT8, top layers FP8/FP16; this mixed configuration recovers most regression while preserving ~50% memory savings.

2025-11-17: Implemented fallback state machine: on decode error or metric delta breach, runtime rematerializes affected KV to INT8/FP16 and replays decode for that request. Prototype increases tail latency but prevents visible bad outputs.
2025-11-19: Human eval (150 pairs) for conversational prompts comparing FP16 baseline vs mixed config: human preference moved 2% in favor of baseline; not statistically significant (p=0.12).
results_summary: Memory: FP8 reduces KV footprint ~58% median, INT8 ~52%, INT4 ~70% with packing. Latency/throughput: at 8-token burst, FP8 mixed config yields +18% token/sec vs FP16 baseline; INT4 aggressive microbench yields +35% but with higher variance. Quality: automated metrics show small regressions (FP8 median +0.02 nats/token, INT8 +0.06, INT4 +0.25). Human eval shows minor preference towards FP16 baseline for aggressive INT4 only; mixed configs are within noise. Failures: INT4 causes deterministic failure modes in math/structured-output prompts; resolved by per-layer protection and runtime fallback.
decisions: Adopt mixed-precision per-layer defaults for rollout: lower 6 layers -> INT4, middle layers -> INT8, top 4 layers -> FP8/FP16 for model families tested. This balances memory gains and quality.
Ship adaptive fallback prototype in runtime-1.18 behind an experimental flag. Default behavior is conservative (no quant) for new customer accounts; opt-in for Dedicated hosts and advanced users.
Delay aggressive INT4-only profile for hosted API until we have larger human eval sweep and better numeric checks in kernel ops.
next_steps: 1) Expand human preference pool to 1k comparisons focusing on math and structured output categories (estimate 2 weeks).
2) Work with kernel team (ENG-33156) to harden FP8 load/store kernels and ensure no denorm flushing edge cases on older GPUs.
3) Add per-model model-card heuristics that recommend default quant profiles and expose toggles in console (runtime + console teams).
4) Optimize packing alignment to reduce INT4 padding waste and re-run cost-per-token simulation for hosted pricing impact.
5) Prepare a runbook: how to detect quant-induced regressions in production and an automated rollback playbook for safety.
